name: Alaska Native Heritage Center
unique: A campus with life size village sites for each Alaska Native culture, from Iñupiat sod houses to a Tlingit clan house, with artists working and dancers performing.
buzz: The village sites and the dance performances are the reasons to come; it is the best introduction to Alaska's Native cultures before you travel anywhere else in the state.

name: Tony Knowles Coastal Trail
unique: An 11 mile paved path along Cook Inlet from downtown to Kincaid Park, with moose in the woods, beluga whales offshore and a view of Mount Susitna.
buzz: Locals bike it after work and the moose are a real hazard on the wooded sections; the tide flats at low tide are the birding.

name: Museum of the North
unique: A curved white building holding a 36,000 year old mummified bison, Alaska Native art and a sound room where you can hear the aurora translated into audio.
buzz: The blue bison and the art galleries are the highlights and the architecture is the photograph; the aurora room is the surprise.

name: Running Reindeer Ranch
unique: A family ranch where a herd of reindeer walks with you through the boreal forest, with a tour that explains antlers, lichen and what reindeer actually are.
buzz: The walk with the herd is the reason people book and the owners are funny and specific; it is a small operation and fills weeks ahead.

name: Alaska State Museum
unique: A museum with a two story Tlingit clan house, a Russian era gallery and a room of Alaska Native basketry, plus a mine and fishing exhibit.
buzz: The clan house and the Russian collection are the two stops; it is a good rainy day in a town that gets a lot of rain.

name: Mount Roberts Tramway
unique: A gondola from the cruise dock to 1,800 feet on Mount Roberts, with trails into the alpine and a view over the channel and the Mendenhall valley.
buzz: The ride is the easy view and the trail at the top is the way to escape the cruise crowd; the mountain is often in cloud.

name: Juneau Whale Watching
unique: A boat into Favorite Channel or Stephens Passage where humpbacks feed in summer, with a naturalist and a hydrophone to hear them.
buzz: The bubble net feeding is the thing people hope for and the hydrophone is the surprise; the boats are small and the water can be rough.

name: Homer Spit
unique: A four and a half mile sand spit into Kachemak Bay lined with charter boats, fish cleaning tables, campgrounds and a view of glaciers across the water.
buzz: The halibut charters and the fish and chips are the local rituals; the spit is busy in summer and the weather changes fast.

name: Halibut Charter from Homer
unique: A day on Cook Inlet or Kachemak Bay pulling halibut that can weigh 100 pounds, with the catch processed and shipped home.
buzz: The fishing is the reason people plan a whole trip and the water can be rough; book early, the good captains fill a year out.

name: Hatcher Pass
unique: A mountain pass above treeline with a road to 3,000 feet, trails to alpine lakes and the ruins of a gold mine, an hour from Anchorage.
buzz: The drive to the pass and the April ski season are the local secrets; the road is rough and the weather turns quickly.

name: Independence Mine
unique: A gold mining camp at 3,500 feet in Hatcher Pass, with bunkhouses, a mill and tram towers still standing against the alpine tundra.
buzz: The buildings against the mountains are the photograph and the rangers explain the mining; the road up is steep and the site is only open in summer.

name: Misty Fjords Flightseeing
unique: A floatplane over the granite walls and waterfalls of Misty Fjords National Monument, landing on a remote lake if the weather allows.
buzz: The lake landing is the reason to pay for the longer trip and the scale of the fjords from the air is the memory; fog cancels flights often.

name: Totem Bight State Park
unique: A clan house and a dozen totem poles in a forest by the sea, carved in the 1930s and 40s as a works project and moved here from abandoned villages.
buzz: The poles and the clan house are the reason to come and the trail is short; the rain forest setting is half the experience.

name: Sitka National Historical Park
unique: The site of the 1804 battle between the Tlingit and the Russians, with a trail through totem poles and a Russian bishop's house.
buzz: The totem trail through the spruce forest is the walk and the visitor center explains the battle; the poles are original and weathered.

name: Alaska Raptor Center
unique: A rehabilitation center with bald eagles, hawks and owls in flight pens, where the staff explain why most of the birds cannot be released.
buzz: The bald eagles are close enough to see the detail and the flight training is the highlight; it is a working hospital and the birds come first.

name: Fort Abercrombie State Park
unique: A World War II coastal defense post on a spruce covered point, with gun emplacements, a lake and a trail along the cliffs.
buzz: The bunkers in the moss are strange and photogenic and the tidepools are good; the weather is usually wet.

name: Kodiak National Wildlife Refuge
unique: An island refuge with 3,500 Kodiak brown bears, salmon streams and a visitor center with mounted bears and a education gallery.
buzz: The flight to a salmon stream to watch bears is the splurge and the visitor center is free; book through a licensed operator and keep your distance.

name: Nome Iditarod Finish
unique: The burled arch at the end of the 1,000 mile Iditarod trail, where the mushers arrive after ten days and the town of 3,700 turns out.
buzz: The finish line in the dark and cold is the experience and the town is welcoming; getting to Nome in March takes planning.

name: Carrie M. McLain Memorial Museum
unique: A museum of the gold rush, the serum run and Iñupiat life on the Seward Peninsula, with photos and objects from the 1898 stampede.
buzz: The serum run and gold rush exhibits are the reason to stop and the staff are local; it is small and warms you up on a cold day.

name: White Pass and Yukon Route
unique: A narrow gauge railroad built during the Klondike gold rush, climbing 3,000 feet from Skagway over the pass into Canada, with a trestle and a view of the gorge.
buzz: The climb past the falls and the abandoned trestles is the reason to ride; the steam trains run on select days and the cars are heated.

name: Klondike Gold Rush National Historical Park
unique: The restored gold rush town and the Chilkoot trailhead, with ranger walks through the wooden buildings and a museum on the stampeders who climbed the pass.
buzz: The ranger walk through town is the best hour in Skagway and the trailhead is a short drive; the town is busy when ships are in.

name: Denali Bus Tour
unique: A school bus ride 60 miles into the park to see grizzlies, wolves, caribou and the mountain itself, the only way past the private vehicle limit.
buzz: The mountain is visible about one day in three and the bus driver is the guide; book the furthest destination you can and bring food.

name: Denali Sled Dog Kennels
unique: The park's working sled dog kennel, where rangers demonstrate a team pulling a cart and explain how dogs still patrol the wilderness in winter.
buzz: The dogs are the highlight for children and the ranger talk is genuinely interesting; the kennel is at the end of a short road from the visitor center.

name: Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes
unique: The ash filled valley left by the 1912 Novarupta eruption, the largest of the 20th century, reached by a bus and a trail across a river and into the ash.
buzz: The scale of the ash valley is the thing and the hike is exposed and remote; book the bus from Brooks Camp well ahead.

name: Kalaupapa Overlook
unique: A overlook 1,600 feet above the leprosy settlement peninsula where Father Damien worked, with the sea cliffs and the village below.
buzz: The view is the reason to drive up and the history is the reason to go down; the settlement itself is only accessible by tour, mule or trail.
